principles.statement: For max clique on graphs with N <= 1000, BBMC-style bitset coloring (independent-set extraction via bitset AND/complement) is dramatically faster than pairwise O(n^2) sequential greedy coloring, enabling the BnB to solve instances that otherwise timeout.
principles.regime: Undirected graphs, N <= 1000, M <= 500000, 2-second time limit
principles.mechanism: Pairwise coloring checks each vertex against all previously colored vertices (O(n^2) comparisons). BBMC coloring extracts independent sets using Q &= ~adj[v] which processes 64 vertices per word operation, reducing the constant factor by ~64x for MAXN=1001.
principles.applicability_bounds: Applies when candidate sets are large (>100 vertices). For small candidate sets the overhead of bitset operations may not pay off vs simple array checks.

principles.statement: Greedy clique construction with 5000 random restarts achieves ~92% of optimal on the test distribution, but BnB with BBMC coloring achieves 100%.
principles.regime: Max clique problem #185 test distribution, N <= 1000
principles.mechanism: Greedy restarts sample many random vertex orderings, finding cliques reachable by greedy extension. BnB exhaustively searches the space (pruned by coloring bounds), finding cliques that require non-greedy vertex selections.
principles.applicability_bounds: The 92% figure is specific to this test distribution. On adversarial graphs (e.g., Keller graphs), greedy could perform much worse.

principles.statement: On the problem-185 test distribution with N<=1000, BnB with greedy coloring bound completes within 1900ms under normal system load, achieving score 100 without needing local search. The iter-1 observed variance (90-100) was caused by system load, not algorithmic timeout.
principles.regime: problem-185 test distribution, N<=1000, M<=500000, normal system load (no heavy background processes)
principles.mechanism: The BnB with greedy coloring bound (solution.cpp:18-80 in iter-2 v4, or expand() in iter-1) explores the search tree efficiently enough to find the optimal clique on all test cases within 1900ms when the system is not under contention. The 1800ms timeout leaves sufficient margin.
principles.applicability_bounds: May not hold under heavy system load — iter-1 showed a score of 90 in one run, likely from load-induced timeout. The local search provides insurance against this failure mode.

principles.statement: Swap-based local search (1-remove/2-add + random perturbation) provides defensive value against BnB timeout but is not necessary for score 100 under normal conditions on the problem-185 test distribution.
principles.regime: problem-185 test distribution, BnB timeout at 1800ms, local search budget 100ms
evidence: iteration-2-h-control-negative: 5/5 runs scored 100 without local search
principles.mechanism: Local search activates only when BnB sets timed_out=true (solution.cpp:308). Under normal load, BnB completes within 1800ms, so local search never runs. Its value is as insurance: when system load causes BnB to timeout, local search can recover using the remaining ~100ms budget.
principles.applicability_bounds: The defensive value becomes critical under system load. The 100ms local search budget is tight — if both BnB and local search are starved for time, scores may still drop.
